posts.text: The US job market is losing workers at an alarming pace: The US labor force participation rate fell -0.1 percentage point in July, to 61.4%, the lowest since May 2020. This metric measures the proportion of working-age Americans either employed or actively looking for work. Excluding the 2020 pandemic, this is the lowest reading since March 1976. The decrease also marks the 7th monthly decline over the last 8 months, bringing the cumulative drop to -1.1 percentage points. This comes as -264,000 people left the labor force in July, following June's -720,000 decline, the 2nd-largest monthly decline since 2020. Since November, the US labor force has shrunk by more than -2.4 million workers. The US job market is much weaker under the surface than the headline data suggests.
posts.author: KobeissiLetter
